title: Rehearsal (friendly client): Maison Verlaine headless e-commerce · Maison Verlaine SA

client.label: Client (simulated)
client.job: Plays the client from their own email: budget, deadline, priorities, a hidden ceiling.

negotiator.label: Empower Negotiator
negotiator.job: Chooses model, scope, discount and concessions; never types a price.

referee.label: Referee
referee.job: Code: prices every offer with the Deal Desk calculator and enforces discount and margin rules.

coach.label: Sales Coach
coach.job: Reads the rehearsal, including the client's private thoughts, and writes the call plan.
coach.summary: The client accepted €6,600 fixed-fee discovery, but this is a discovery win—not approval of the build; use discovery to validate whether all must-haves can credibly launch before Valentine’s Day.

data.message: Thanks for the proposal. The full scope is close to what we had in mind, but an estimated T&M engagement at this price leaves us exposed, and a March 11 go-live misses our ideal Valentine’s Day window. Could you propose a committed first phase that includes all the must-haves and gets us live before Valentine’s Day, with clearer cost control?
objections: March 11 go-live misses Valentine’s Day target
data.private_thoughts: Price is near my expected range, so I would not push hard on the headline number yet; I need delivery before Valentine's and reduced cost risk. A phased, capped/ fixed-fee first release retaining headless catalogue, checkout and payments, gifts, corporate orders, and Odoo integration could close.

trace.text: Round 0: negotiating (T&M estimate creates budget uncertainty; March 11 go-live misses Valentine’s Day target)

data.message: A committed all-must-have first phase cannot responsibly be promised before Valentine’s Day: our current delivery plan reaches go-live in March, and we still need to resolve key scope and specialist-capability questions. I recommend starting with paid discovery on a T&M basis, with defined outputs covering those open questions, specialist confirmation, and a validated schedule; we can then provide a fixed build quote with documented assumptions and change control. If you’re comfortable proceeding, let’s align on prompt discovery sign-off and timely access to your team so we can assess whether the Valentine’s target is achievable.
concessions: Discovery deliverables to include resolution of open requirements, specialist capability confirmation, and an evidence-based delivery schedule; fixed build quote follows.
data.internal_reasoning: Client’s request for a guaranteed complete first phase by Valentine’s conflicts with the calculated delivery plan and no Phase 1 scope exists. The paid discovery is the honest negotiated move to address material uncertainty and rebaseline, without discounting in the absence of budget or competitive pressure; ask for prompt sign-off and client availability in return.

data.message: The discovery scope and two-week turnaround sound useful, but I’m hesitant to approve it as open-ended T&M without a clear cap and a commitment to the outputs, especially the validated schedule and fixed build quote. Please make the discovery fee fixed or capped at the stated amount, and confirm that the 2026-11-09 deliverables will let us make a go/no-go decision on a Valentine’s launch, including any risks to that date. If you can do that, I’m prepared to move quickly on access and sign-off.
objections: Discovery is T&M with no explicit cost cap
data.private_thoughts: This is a sensible smaller first step, and the fee itself is acceptable if capped. I do not want to commit to a larger build until the date and full must-have scope are validated; a fixed build quote and credible Valentine’s plan would keep us engaged.

trace.text: Round 1: negotiating (Discovery is T&M with no explicit cost cap; Valentine’s feasibility remains uncommitted)

data.message: We can make the discovery a fixed-fee engagement, with the agreed two-week outputs delivered by November 9: resolved scope questions, confirmation of specialist coverage, and a validated delivery plan with a clear go/no-go assessment of the Valentine’s launch and its risks. Please provide timely access to the relevant stakeholders and approve the discovery promptly; the build quote will then be fixed, with assumptions and change control documented.
concessions: Fixed fee for discovery with the stated deliverables and two-week turnaround, contingent on prompt access and sign-off.
data.internal_reasoning: Client's second objection explicitly asks for capped cost and committed outputs; switching to fixed discovery answers that directly without unnecessary discount. The full build cannot meet Valentine's under the current plan, so discovery should transparently establish feasibility rather than promise the date.

data.message: The fixed fee and explicit go/no-go assessment by November 9 address my main concerns, and I can move quickly on access and sign-off. Please make sure the fixed build quote and validated schedule clearly cover the agreed must-haves, with any assumptions or risks to a pre-Valentine’s launch stated plainly. I’m ready to proceed with discovery on that basis.
data.private_thoughts: Discovery at EUR 6,600 is acceptable given the fixed fee, concrete deliverables, and timely decision point; it is not a commitment to the eventual build. I’d want the fixed build quote for all must-haves close to my expected range, with a credible plan for pre-Valentine’s go-live.

data.headline: The client accepted €6,600 fixed-fee discovery, but this is a discovery win—not approval of the build; use discovery to validate whether all must-haves can credibly launch before Valentine’s Day.
likely_objections: A March 11 full-scope go-live misses the client’s ideal February 14 date; the client wants a credible date assessment, not an unsupported promise.
The original €80,300 T&M estimate leaves the client exposed to cost uncertainty; they want capped cost and committed outputs.
The client will judge the eventual fixed build quote against its expected range and wants it to cover all must-haves.
concession_path: Start with the accepted €6,600 fixed-fee, two-week discovery, contingent on prompt sign-off and stakeholder access; commit to the November 9 outputs: resolved scope questions, specialist coverage confirmation, and a validated schedule with a Valentine’s go/no-go and risks.

After discovery, present a fixed build quote for the agreed must-haves with explicit assumptions, exclusions, and change control, alongside a schedule grounded in confirmed requirements and specialist availability.
If the build price is a concern, first explore scope or delivery trade-offs only if the client confirms which must-haves or timing priorities can change; do not discount speculatively.
data.walk_away_point: Do not promise a pre-Valentine’s launch or commit to fixed build pricing before discovery resolves the open scope and specialist questions. If the client requires those guarantees without a credible validated plan, pause rather than sell an unworkable commitment.
what_worked: The negotiator directly addressed the deadline and uncertainty instead of pretending the March 11 plan met the client’s goal.
Switching discovery from T&M to a €6,600 fixed fee, with explicit deliverables and a November 9 decision point, answered the client’s stated condition and secured acceptance.
The negotiator tied the concession to prompt access and sign-off.
what_to_avoid: Do not treat discovery acceptance as agreement to the build; the client explicitly said they are not yet committing to it.
Do not imply discovery will make Valentine’s feasible. Promise a transparent go/no-go assessment and risks, not the date itself.
The initial discovery offer was described as T&M even though a €5,900 amount was stated; avoid ambiguity about whether a price is capped or estimated.
questions_to_ask: Can you provide timely access to the decision-makers and the teams needed to close the eight open requirements and validate Odoo, Bancontact, and Magento coverage?
For the February 14 target, what launch risks or trade-offs are acceptable, and is that date a firm requirement or an ideal?
When we return with the build quote, what budget range or approval limit should we design to, and who will approve it?
